nodes.Name: tmpStringBufSize
nodes.DocComment:
The constant is known to the compiler.
There is no fundamental theory behind this number.

nodes.Name: concatstrings
nodes.DocComment:
concatstrings implements a Go string concatenation x+y+z+...
The operands are passed in the slice a.
If buf != nil, the compiler has determined that the result does not
escape the calling function, so the string data can be stored in buf
if small enough.

nodes.Name: concatstring2
nodes.DocComment:
concatstring2 helps make the callsite smaller (compared to concatstrings),
and we think this is currently more valuable than omitting one call in the
chain, the same goes for concatstring{3,4,5}.

nodes.Name: concatbytes
nodes.DocComment:
concatbytes implements a Go string concatenation x+y+z+... returning a slice
of bytes.
The operands are passed in the slice a.

nodes.Name: concatbyte2
nodes.DocComment:
concatbyte2 helps make the callsite smaller (compared to concatbytes),
and we think this is currently more valuable than omitting one call in
the chain, the same goes for concatbyte{3,4,5}.

nodes.Name: slicebytetostring
nodes.DocComment:
slicebytetostring converts a byte slice to a string.
It is inserted by the compiler into generated code.
ptr is a pointer to the first element of the slice;
n is the length of the slice.
Buf is a fixed-size buffer for the result,
it is not nil if the result does not escape.

nodes.Name: stringDataOnStack
nodes.DocComment:
stringDataOnStack reports whether the string's data is
stored on the current goroutine's stack.

nodes.Name: slicebytetostringtmp
nodes.DocComment:
slicebytetostringtmp returns a "string" referring to the actual []byte bytes.

Callers need to ensure that the returned string will not be used after
the calling goroutine modifies the original slice or synchronizes with
another goroutine.

The function is only called when instrumenting
and otherwise intrinsified by the compiler.

Some internal compiler optimizations use this function.
  - Used for m[T1{... Tn{..., string(k), ...} ...}] and m[string(k)]
    where k is []byte, T1 to Tn is a nesting of struct and array literals.
  - Used for "<"+string(b)+">" concatenation where b is []byte.
  - Used for string(b)=="foo" comparison where b is []byte.

nodes.Name: stringStructDWARF
nodes.DocComment: Variant with *byte pointer type for DWARF debugging.

nodes.Name: rawstring
nodes.DocComment:
rawstring allocates storage for a new string. The returned
string and byte slice both refer to the same storage.
The storage is not zeroed. Callers should use
b to set the string contents and then drop b.

nodes.Name: rawbyteslice
nodes.DocComment: rawbyteslice allocates a new byte slice. The byte slice is not zeroed.

nodes.Name: rawruneslice
nodes.DocComment: rawruneslice allocates a new rune slice. The rune slice is not zeroed.

internal_syscall_gostring is a version of gostring for internal/syscall/unix.

nodes.Name: parseByteCount
nodes.DocComment:
parseByteCount parses a string that represents a count of bytes.

s must match the following regular expression:

	^[0-9]+(([KMGT]i)?B)?$

In other words, an integer byte count with an optional unit
suffix. Acceptable suffixes include one of
- KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB which represent binary IEC/ISO 80000 units, or
- B, which just represents bytes.

Returns an int64 because that's what its callers want and receive,
but the result is always non-negative.
